summary: `/start` surfaced `resume 2026-04-16-branch-hygiene` from a stale run-ledger session entry and caused an unintended scope reopen. The START menu currently treats any ledger session with `status` in `{active, parked}` as resumable, which is too permissive when there is no live approved scope, no parked session-state handoff, and no validated resumable checkpoint for that session.
evidence: On 2026-04-17, the plain welcome output listed `resume 2026-04-16-branch-hygiene` even though that session had already been delivered earlier (ep-210) and was not intended as the next action. `scripts/welcome.py` builds the START resume list from `load_open_sessions()` and prints `resume <session_id>` entries for all open sessions; `scripts/run_ledger.py` defines open sessions as any session with `status` in `{active, parked}`. This allowed a stale `active` ledger row to appear as a fresh resume option.
recommended_action: Tighten the START resume filter so stale `active` ledger rows are not surfaced as resumable by default. When there is no live approved scope and `session-state.md` is not parked, only advertise `resume <session_id>` if the session has an explicit parked handoff or another validated resume signal from the ledger/checkpoint state. Add a focused regression test in `tests/test_welcome.py` covering a stale `active` ledger entry with closed scope/session-state so `/start` does not offer a false-positive resume option.

summary: Azoth lacks a supported way to finalize a bookkeeping-only or already-bumped session without forcing another patch bump. Parking kept the repo moving, but it also occupied the default parked-session slot and created avoidable UX friction in `/resume` and `/start`.
evidence: On 2026-04-17, the ad-hoc closeout follow-up was functionally complete but could not be cleanly closed without running `scripts/do_closeout.py`, which unconditionally calls `version-bump.py --patch`. Leaving it parked solved version churn but created a different coupling: `session-state.md` stayed `state: parked`, so the default resume surface pointed at a dead-end administrative session instead of future real work. Existing docs/tests also codify the bump as mandatory, so there is no supported no-bump finalization path today.
recommended_action: Add an explicit administrative close/finalize path for parked, bookkeeping-only, or already-bumped sessions that updates scope/session registry state to `closed` without W4 patch bump. Document when that path is allowed, wire it into `/park` or `/session-closeout`, and add tests covering default resume behavior after finalizing an administrative parked session.

summary: An eager local fix can still be wrong if it resolves the immediate symptom but introduces a second-order UX coupling that was not evaluated. Parking the residual session removed version churn in the moment, but the design cost to the default parked-session UX was not thought through before applying it.
evidence: The session used parking as a fast hygiene workaround for an administrative follow-up. That choice looked locally correct because it avoided another closeout/version cycle, but it shifted the burden into the resume model: the parked slot became occupied by a non-work session, which makes future `/resume` and `/start` behavior noisier. The issue was not implementation quality; it was incomplete systems thinking around downstream UX coupling before choosing the workaround.
recommended_action: When applying a fast hygiene or governance workaround, explicitly review secondary effects across adjacent session UX surfaces before shipping it: `/start`, `/resume`, parked-session defaults, closeout semantics, and version policy. Capture this as a lightweight pre-implementation checklist item for self-improvement so local fixes are screened for cross-surface coupling before they harden into workflow debt.
